sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: 'Quality Checks' row 48 and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 48 (no internal annotation on row 48), cell comments scanned
task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (users, jobs, applications, messages, reads parsed)
task/tests/test.sh lines 195-230 (app_context injection, run_suite, suite order)
evidence:
Residue search: no sibling product name, foreign account list, foreign data shape, template CHANGE_ME, or unfilled placeholder in any of the five prompts, the injected app_context or the criteria. Grep over task/tests *.md/*.toml for colderwater/ledger/clinic/warehouse/invoice/ticket/patient/inventory/tenant/shipment/admin@/example.com/password123/TODO/TBD/lorem/placeholder returned nothing; the only brace tokens are {app_context} and {criteria}, which test.sh:195-200 and rewardkit fill. tests/app_context.md:3 'Name: HireOps' replaces the template's CHANGE_ME (template app_context.md:3,8,12).

Credentials: app_context.md:8-19 lists password 'Hireops!2026' and all 10 accounts with roles. These match instruction.md:17, hireops_rules.md:11 and seed_data.json users (USR-REC1..3 Rafael Costa/Mei Lin/Farah Nasser recruiters; USR-MGR1..3 Ingrid Sorensen/Bill Okafor/Yuki Tanaka hiring_manager; USR-OBS1 Aud Halvorsen observer; USR-CAN1..3 Noor Haddad/Tomas Varga/Lena Fischer candidates). Every person named in the prompts and criteria (Rafael, Mei Lin, Ingrid, Bill, Aud, Noor, Tomas) exists with the role the prompt assigns.

Screens and entities: app_context.md:23-25 (Board with Applied/Screen/Interview/Offer/Hired/Rejected, Conversations, Activity, candidate applications view) matches instruction.md:11 and hireops_rules.md §3, §4, §6 and §7. The candidate wording in hro_candidate_view matches the rules §7 table exactly. The page size of 30 in hro_thread_latest and hro_thread_earlier matches rules §6. The 1-50 whole-number places behind the 0/51/2.5 refusals in protocol S match rules §2. The 15-second live window matches instruction.md:5 and rules §5. The 401/403/404 semantics in hro_anonymous and protocol K match rules §1.

Seeded facts cited in prompts were re-derived from seed_data.json. There are three jobs (Platform Engineer, Data Analyst, Product Designer), matching app_context.md:29. APP-101 Noor/Platform Engineer has exactly 120 messages, matching app_context.md:30, functional T/U and polish lines 14/16. Noor also has APP-302 (Product Designer), so naming the 'Platform Engineer conversation' correctly disambiguates it. For APP-201 Tomas/Data Analyst, Mei Lin (USR-REC2) has read_count 1 of 3 and messages 2-3 are from USR-CAN2, so her unread count is 2. That matches functional prompt.md:39 and hro_unread_counts. Visual prompt.md:14 says 'a seeded job with cards in several stages': JOB-PLAT has Applied 3, Screen 2, Interview 2 and Offer 1.

Internal consistency: gate prompts (render prompt.md:9, constraints prompt.md:9) agree with their single criteria hro_gate_render and hro_gate_shared. In the functional prompt, every criterion's protocol letter (S, M, L, C, B, N, T, U, K, R, V, A, D) maps to an existing protocol section, and role facts agree: Bill is J2's manager in S and T and in hro_thread_access, and Ingrid is J1's manager in S, N and R and in hro_mgr_*. The polish prompt's 'workable order' (line 16) names rows that exist: live-board, the conversation rows on Noor's conversation, failed-send and ended-session. Its tool guidance (lines 14) agrees with hro_pol_failed_send and hro_pol_session_resume. The visual prompt (lines 12-14) agrees with five likert criteria that all have anchors 1-5. The deliverable described everywhere is the HireOps recruiting workspace at http://localhost:3000. That is consistent with instruction.md and is the only app described.

I tried a broken app that could pass: a prompt that claimed false seed facts (for example the wrong unread count or the wrong long-thread owner) would mis-grade a correct app, but every such fact checked out. I tried a conforming app that could fail: the prompts do not name routes, selectors or labels ('Discover routes and controls by intent', app_context.md:33-34, functional prompt.md:15), so no foreign UI shape is imposed.

Non-blocking observations (P3, not defects for this row; recorded for the owner):
(a) functional/judge.toml hro_unread_counts: after Tomas's two new messages, 'Rafael's count for that conversation' grammatically points back to the Data Analyst conversation, but protocol U (prompt.md:39) runs that step on Tomas's conversation from T. The protocol is explicit, so the judge has an unambiguous procedure.
(b) functional prompt.md:37 lets protocol T fall back to 'open a new job J3' without stating that J3's manager must be Bill. 'as Bill (manager of J2)' and 'Ingrid (not J2's manager)' then assume J2. The fallback is practically unreachable because J2 is freshly created in S without Tomas's address.
(c) functional prompt.md:39 says the starting read markers give Mei Lin 2 unread on APP-201. That holds unless an earlier scored dimension sends in or opens APP-201 as Mei. Polish's failed-send and session-resume rows leave the conversation unspecified. Suites run sequentially on one app (test.sh run_suite, --max-concurrent-agent 1), and the dimension order inside rewardkit is not visible in the task. If functional runs first (it is first alphabetically) the claim is exact. Otherwise the claim is accurate only if polish avoids APP-201.
No runtime was performed for this row: it is a source-accuracy check, and no raw-evidence artifact was needed or cited.
